semantic_contract: cEditor member, called only from the editor subsystem, with no arguments and no return value. It detaches and releases the Model* held in the receiver's member at +0xf0. Invariants, in order: (1) if that member is null, do nothing at all; (2) otherwise call IModelWorld slot +0x16c on model->mpWorld with (model, false), which is SetInWorld(model, false), and discard the result; (3) re-read the member, because that call may have cleared it, and return without side effects if it is now null; (4) set the member to null BEFORE any release work, so a re-entrant call sees a null member and cannot double-release; (5) if model->mnRefCount is greater than 1, decrement it and return - the Model survives; (6) otherwise, with no decrement at all, call IModelWorld slot +0x170 on model->mpWorld with (model, bit 31 of model->mFlags), which is FinalRelease. The counter test is CMP 1 / JLE, so a counter of 0 also takes the FinalRelease path. The counter is a plain non-atomic dword; there is no LOCK or XADD anywhere in the body. Every one of the 10 observed call sites gates the call on the one-byte guard at cEditor+0xe9 and clears that guard immediately afterwards, so the routine is idempotent from the caller's point of view and is the teardown half of a load/store pair whose load half is 0x0057a610.
classification_rationale: The whole 92-byte body is read from the disassembly with no unresolved region, every field offset it touches is independently corroborated by two to five separate agreement points with Spore/Graphics/Model.h, both virtual slots map to IModelWorld methods whose declared arity, argument order and even lifetime comment match the observed call shape, and the guard-setter 0x0057e160 plus the setup 0x0057a610 pin the caller's contract. It is not STRONG-with-reservation-free: the semantic name of the cEditor routine, the meaning of mFlags bit 31 and the +0xe9 flag are all withheld because no evidence names them. Those three are naming gaps, not mechanics gaps, and the classification rests on the mechanics.
semantic_findings: The routine is 'hide, detach, then reference-counted release' of one Model* member, and the order matters: the member is nulled at 0x005772d6 before the counter is touched.

Both virtual calls use model->mpWorld as the receiver and pass the model itself as the first stack argument, so the world is the callee and the model is the subject - the opposite of the usual 'ask the model about the world' direction.

The +0x16c call receives the literal 0, i.e. visible == false, and its return value is discarded. The SDK name for that slot, SetInWorld, describes the general operation; the observed argument is specifically the hide direction.

The counter at +0x40 is decremented only when it exceeds 1; when it is 1 or 0 nothing is decremented and the FinalRelease path runs. This is a decrement-or-destroy release, matching the SDK comment that the model destructor calls FinalRelease.
The FinalRelease bool is bit 31 of Model::mFlags, extracted as an unsigned shift then masked to a byte. It is not a sign test, so the raw bit is what is passed.
0x0040f360 is the same release idiom compiled out of line, which is strong independent evidence for the refcount offset, the comparison constant and the 0x170 slot.

The re-read of the member at 0x005772cc and the null check at 0x005772d4 mean the function tolerates the +0x16c call having already released or detached the model; in that case it performs no release of its own.

All 10 call sites discard the return and all of them write 0 to the +0xe9 guard right after, so the function has no observable result and its only externally visible effects are on the model and on the member.
unresolved_questions: What is this routine called in the original source? No string, symbol, PDB reference or vtable entry in the binary names it, and the +0xe9 guard is a bare byte with no SDK counterpart.
What does bit 31 of Model::mFlags (0x80000000) mean? It is undocumented in the SDK Model.h flag enum and in cMWModelInternal::field_138, and no writer of that specific bit was located.

Is the +0xf0 model a 'preview', 'ghost' or 'highlight' model? The setup writes an all-ones mColor and a bitmask derived from an index-returning world call, which is consistent with several editor overlay uses, and nothing observed here decides between them.
Why is EBX saved only on the FinalRelease path? The body never reads EBX for any other purpose, so the save is a register-allocation artefact of the compiler rather than an invariant.
Which concrete IModelWorld implementation receives the +0x16c and +0x170 calls? The vtable is a runtime object and no static table was located for these two sites.

Is the counter at +0x40 really Model::mnRefCount in the original build, or a per-world counter that happens to share the offset? The five-way offset agreement makes this unlikely but nothing at runtime confirms it.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has ever been captured for 0x005772b0, so every claim here is static. A differential trace must confirm that mpWorld is non-null whenever the +0xf0 member is non-null, because both virtual calls dereference model->mpWorld twice with no null check.
A trace must confirm that IModelWorld slot +0x170 does not itself decrement the counter, since this body reaches it with the counter still at 1 (or 0).
A trace with a concrete editor receiver is required before the +0xf0 member and the +0xe9 guard can be given semantic names.
